clue.text: Incompetent with US agency in clear

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it, wrapped by the surrounding letters

blocks.note: someone incompetent is 'not able', run together as one string
Immigration and Customs Enforcement, an American federal agency

explanation.surface: An American agency is accused of being incompetent in plain sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incompetent' must be broken into two words, not able, so the agency can sit between them. ICE is America's immigration enforcement agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Something easily seen or obvious is plainly evident, so it can be described as clear or apparent.

clue.text: English gent elevated getting title

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising letters up the column makes them read from bottom to top

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: An English gentleman is raised to the peerage and gets a title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevated' suggests promotion to a peerage, but in a down entry it means the letters are read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The heading by which a book, film or person is known can be called either its title or its label.

clue.text: Sailor quietly stripped heaving canvas sheet

indicators.note: stripping something removes its outer covering, so the word loses both its end letters

blocks.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
p for piano, the musical direction for quietly
heaving a rope is hauling it

explanation.surface: A sailor quietly hauls on a canvas sheet, as on a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stripped' reads as undressed, but it means peeling off the first and last letters. Tar is an old word for a sailor, from the tarred clothing they wore.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a large waterproof covering, traditionally of tarred canvas, used to protect goods or cover boats.

clue.text: Cots required in babies’ sleep, initially

definitions.text: Cots required in babies’ sleep, initially
definitions.note: the whole clue doubles as the definition

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of each word is used

blocks.note: the first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Babies need somewhere to sleep, so cots are required.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: its initial letters spell the answer, and read straight it describes what cribs are for.
explanation.definitionFit: A crib is the usual American word for a baby's bed with high barred sides, which the British call a cot.

clue.text: American, through experiment, almost flies

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
via means by way of, through
a test is an experiment

explanation.surface: An American pilot learns to fly through trial and error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Through' is not a link here but gives letters of its own, the Latin-derived word meaning by way of.
explanation.definitionFit: To aviate is to pilot an aircraft, so a person who does this is said to fly a plane.

clue.text: In speech, moderates lectures

indicators.note: in speech means as spoken out loud, so we go by sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: to moderate something is to lessen it

explanation.surface: A speaker tones down their lectures when talking.
explanation.walkthrough: LESSENS and LESSONS are pronounced the same in most accents.
explanation.definitionFit: Lessons and lectures are both teaching sessions, and a lecture can also be a telling-off, as a lesson can.

clue.text: Issue from old man’s son

blocks.note: pa is a familiar word for father, the old man, plus the possessive s
standard abbreviation in genealogies

explanation.surface: A son is the issue, or offspring, of his father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like offspring, which fits the family surface, but it is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge may pass sentence or issue a judgment; both verbs mean formally to deliver or pronounce something.

clue.text: Fleet US soldier found in drink

indicators.note: something found in something else is located inside it

blocks.note: GI is the familiar term for an American private soldier
ale is a drink, beer

explanation.surface: An American serviceman from the navy's fleet is discovered drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' reads as a navy noun, but it is the adjective meaning swift.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet of foot means quick and nimble in movement, the same quality described by agile.

clue.text: Counting following small, small amount

indicators.note: following means coming after, which fixes which part goes second

blocks.note: standard abbreviation, as on clothing labels
to count is to matter or be important

explanation.surface: Someone counting tiny sums one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' appears twice: the first is the abbreviation, the second belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A smattering is a slight scattering or a superficial knowledge, a little of something rather than much.

clue.text: She reportedly needs others to work

definitions.text: She reportedly needs others to work

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so a word is to be heard rather than read

blocks.clueFragment: She reportedly needs others to work
blocks.note: surface reading: a woman who depends on other people to do the work for her
setter's reading: heard aloud the word could equally be spelt 'kneads', so she kneads other people as her job

explanation.surface: A woman who supposedly lets others do all the work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' tells you to hear 'needs' as 'kneads': she kneads others for a living.
explanation.definitionFit: A female practitioner of massage works by kneading clients' muscles, so others are what her work is done on.

clue.text: Spoil one purchasing can for drink

indicators.note: purchasing means taking in or acquiring, so one part takes the other inside it

blocks.note: to mar is to spoil
the Roman numeral
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Someone buying a can of drink spoils the occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Spoil one' as a single unit that does the purchasing, so the can goes between its last two letters rather than after them.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth, so it is a kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Fires back lacking energy and strength

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, so the word is read right to left
lacking means without, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: to fire someone up is to animate them
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone retaliates but is short of energy and strength.
explanation.walkthrough: ANIMATES read backwards is SETAMINA; take out the E and STAMINA remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, the physical or mental endurance to keep going, which is a form of strength.

clue.text: Very high plunge nearly leading contest

indicators.note: nearly means not quite complete, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: a plunge is a fall
a set-to is a fight or contest

explanation.surface: A dramatic high dive puts someone ahead in a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very high' looks like a description of the plunge, but it defines a singing voice. A set-to is a squabble or bout.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto describes a male voice pitched far above its natural range, so the word fits a very high register.

clue.text: End of Scrubs’ prison time done

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: last letter of the word
pen is short for penitentiary
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A prisoner at Wormwood Scrubs finishes their sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: Wormwood Scrubs is a London prison, which makes 'prison time done' read as one phrase about release.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in the sense of exhausted or used up, like a spent force or a spent match.

clue.text: Authority oddly sapped US agency record

indicators.note: oddly means in the odd positions, so the first, third and fifth letters are kept

blocks.note: letters one, three and five
the Central Intelligence Agency
to list is to record

explanation.surface: An American intelligence agency's records drain authority in strange ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Authority' reads as power, but here it means a person who knows a subject thoroughly.
explanation.definitionFit: An authority on a subject is an expert who knows it deeply, which is what a specialist is.

clue.text: Beds sweethearts accepting everything

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one part goes inside the other

blocks.note: pet is a term of endearment
all means everything

explanation.surface: A lover who sleeps with sweethearts and takes on everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beds' looks like a verb about seduction, but it is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A pallet is a straw mattress or makeshift bed on the floor, so pallets are crude places to sleep.

clue.text: Shocking vote for costly cut

indicators.note: cut means trimmed short, so the final letter is lopped off

blocks.note: to elect is to vote in
rich can mean expensive, as rich fare

explanation.surface: A scandalous vote in favour of expensive budget cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' sounds like a budget cut in the surface but just trims a letter. Rich food or rich prices are costly ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Something electric can give an electric shock, and it also describes a thrilling, startling atmosphere.

clue.text: More like dressing, or less dressed?

blocks.note: first meaning: closer to a sauce, as a salad dressing is
second meaning: more risqué or cheeky, wearing less

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' and 'dressed' seem to be about clothes both times; the first is a salad dressing, a kind of sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative works as 'more sauce-like' and as 'more cheeky or risqué', as with a racy outfit.

clue.text: Simple men tempted to acquire gadget

indicators.note: to acquire is to take in and hold, so the phrase holds the letters within it

blocks.note: found running across the three words

explanation.surface: Gullible men are lured into buying a gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from inside 'Simple' through 'men' to the first letter of 'tempted'.
explanation.definitionFit: An implement is a tool or utensil, and a gadget is a small handy device of the same kind.

clue.text: Soundly beats children’s game

indicators.note: soundly here means by sound, so we listen rather than read

blocks.note: to beat is to conquer

explanation.surface: Someone thoroughly defeats opponents at a playground game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like 'thoroughly'. Conkers is a British game where children swing horse chestnuts on strings to smash an opponent's.
explanation.definitionFit: Conkers is the name of the traditional schoolchildren's game played with chestnuts threaded on string.

clue.text: Doctor fish discharging last of milt

indicators.note: discharging means letting out, so a letter is expelled
the last of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: a sturgeon is a large fish
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fish releasing milt, its sperm, attended by a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: STURGEON with its T removed gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is a medical practitioner who operates, so is a kind of doctor.

clue.text: Degrade Church name taking Mass

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the pair surrounds what follows

blocks.note: the Church of England
standard abbreviation
a mass is a heap

explanation.surface: A church brings its name into disrepute by saying Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' has a capital to suggest the church service; it is simply a large amount, wrapped by CE and N.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheapen something is to lower its worth or dignity, which is to degrade it.

clue.text: Fitting wearing correct collar

indicators.note: something wearing a garment is inside it, so one part is covered by the other

blocks.note: apt means fitting
to correct a fault is to cure it

explanation.surface: Trying on a shirt to see whether its collar fits properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collar' looks like part of a shirt but is the informal verb for arresting someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Police slang to collar a suspect means to seize or arrest them, which is to take them prisoner.

clue.text: Check trailer’s front behind car

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter
behind means following after, setting the order of the parts

blocks.note: Audi is a make of car
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone checks the front of a trailer hitched behind a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The T goes behind the make of car.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an official inspection of accounts or records, so it is a formal check.

clue.text: Bird beginning to display comb

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: first letter of the word
to rake is to comb through

explanation.surface: A bird starts to show off its comb, like a cockerel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comb' looks like a cockerel's crest but is the verb, as in raking through.
explanation.definitionFit: A drake is a male duck, so the answer is a particular kind of bird.

clue.text: Left inside, grass grassed?

indicators.note: inside means within, so one part sits in the middle of the other

blocks.note: port is the left side of a ship
a reed is a tall grass

explanation.surface: A wordplay joke: grass, once mown, has been 'grassed' inside.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang to grass is to inform on someone to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To grass on someone is slang for informing the authorities about them, that is, reporting them.

clue.text: Fast driver reversing vehicle over Queen!

indicators.note: reversing means going backwards, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A speeding motorist backs over the Queen, to general alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen; in a down clue 'over' puts RAC above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A racer is someone who competes in races, such as a racing driver who goes at high speed.

clue.text: Endlessly disgusting filth

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: crude can mean vulgar or disgusting

explanation.surface: Grime that is disgusting without end.
explanation.walkthrough: CRUDE loses its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Crud is informal for dirt or grime, a nasty deposit, so it means filth.

clue.text: Fancy one finding silver in excavation!

indicators.note: in means inside, so one part is placed within another

blocks.note: the Roman numeral
a mine is an excavation
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Fancy that, someone striking silver in a dig!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' is the exclamation of surprise, used as the verb meaning to picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy that something is so is to imagine or suppose it, an older sense of the verb.

clue.text: Vague relative warm at heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letters are kept

blocks.note: an uncle is a relative
the two central letters

explanation.surface: A vague relative who is kindly underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: UNCLE is followed by the middle of 'warm'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vague is not clearly expressed or understood, so it is indistinct and hazy.

clue.text: Constraint with run on bank

blocks.note: a tie is a restriction or binding obligation
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Financial restrictions combined with a run on a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run on bank' sounds like a financial panic; 'on' just puts R after TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a row or level, as in banked rows of seats, and a bank of things is such a row.

clue.text: United from inside target niftily turned

indicators.note: taking letters from a phrase means they are lifted straight out of the words that follow
turned round means facing the other way, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: the letters span the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A football club such as United, nimbly turning inside to target goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Niftily turned' looks like an anagram signal, but this setter avoids anagrams: the letters sit in 'insiDE TARGET NIftily' and read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Integrated means combined into a whole, joined together as one, so it is a synonym of united.
